newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Semis - Comfortable at tight spreads.
newsitem.headline: Australian Semis - Comfortable at tight spreads.

text.p: *Semis spreads to Australian government debt remained in a narrow trading range with the market seen as comfortable with the tighter differentials since the changes to bank's PAR.

Semis yield spreads to Australian government securities remained in a narrow trading range with the market seen as comfortable with the tighter differentials since the change in commerical bank's prudential requirements.

The change in par asset ratios (PAR) announced by the Reserve Bank earlier this month, and which came into effect last Monday, now include semi-government securities, but also saw a reduction in PAR to 3.0 from 6.0 percent.
"Semis are quiet, but look fairly comfortable at the tighter levels. If they widen one or two basis points there are plenty of buyers around," said one trader at European bank in Sydney.
"Equally if they narrow any more there is going to be profit-taking," the trader added.

Traders said domestic institutions had been looking to take up short-dated stocks, although most of the interest in the semis market had occured in the run-up and on the confirmation of the change in PAR requirements.

Overall Australian debt markets have been restricted to limited interest in the past week with little local data to trade against and as they await next week's policy making meetings in Australia and the U.S.

A 50 basis point cut in Australia's official 5.5 percent interest rate is more or less priced in for after the Reserve Bank board meeting on July 1, although such a move is seen as dependent on the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 and 2 keeping U.S. interest rates on hold.
